analysis_status: designed after the repaired current-state opportunity result was inspected; robustness/ecological decomposition only, not confirmatory
question: Within the clean current-year marginal opportunity model, do plant flowering availability and pollinator activity on other plants contribute differently to gain and loss discrimination?

increment_definitions.plant_availability_increment: pollinator_only held-out log-loss minus marginal_full held-out log-loss
increment_definitions.pollinator_activity_increment: plant_only held-out log-loss minus marginal_full held-out log-loss

preprocessing: log1p and training-fold z-score, identical to the repaired opportunity baseline
cross_validation: same strict-core, near-core and all-annual leave-one-transition-out response holdouts

classification_rule.reproducible_incremental_information: pooled drop-one-axis log-loss penalty is positive and positive in every held-out transition in the declared scope
classification_rule.positive_but_fold_unstable: pooled penalty is positive but at least one held-out transition is non-positive

interpretation.allowed: retrospective predictive-information asymmetry between plant-side availability and pollinator-side activity
forbidden: pollinator behavior as the demonstrated cause of gain
plant phenology as the demonstrated cause of loss

claim_ceiling: This audit can show which marginal current-state opportunity axis carries more held-out predictive information for each endpoint. Because it was motivated after the repaired result was seen and both axes are measured through the observational sampling process, it is descriptive and hypothesis-generating rather than causal or confirmatory.
